extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant reviewers and infectious-disease/microbiology researchers preparing or evaluating animal-model grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: A research strategy section of an NIH-style grant proposing development and characterization of a mouse model of enteric Burkholderia pseudomallei infection, including aims, experimental approaches, endpoints, animal use, and biosafety compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance of a new enteric Bp animal model
rubrics_metrics.description: Development of a new animal model of enteric Bp infection would be valuable for understanding pathogenesis of enteric melioidosis, for study of enteric pathogens generally, and for development of new vaccines and antimicrobial treatment/prevention strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains clinical and scientific value: essential to understand human pathogenesis, adds a new animal model for enteric pathogens, critical for vaccine and antimicrobial development. Emphasizes novelty given almost no prior knowledge of enteric Bp infection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (novel observations and tools)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unexpected observation that mice can be infected orally with Bp, persistently shed Bp fecally, and show mouse strain differences in susceptibility; development of a new enteric infection model that may alter the Bp infection paradigm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites access to a panel of >30 clinical isolates and the development of a modified Ashdown’s selective medium as technical innovations that enable these studies and support novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data supporting feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior studies showed oral infection and persistent fecal shedding in mice, strain-dependent susceptibility, enteric virulence across clinical isolates, and availability of modified selective medium to culture Bp from intestinal contents and feces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes how preliminary animal-challenge data and the selective medium justify the proposed aims and reduce risk of the experimental plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall experimental approach and aim-driven structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Aims 1–3 with clear objectives: screen 30 clinical isolates for enteric tropism/virulence; correlate enteric virulence with cell invasion/replication assays; identify intestinal target cells; determine mechanisms of dissemination from GI tract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach includes defined animal models, in vitro assays, use of GFP/RFP-labeled bacteria, confocal microscopy and flow cytometry, and specific experimental timelines and sample sizes; describes rationale and hypotheses for each aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary in vivo readouts/endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary readouts for challenge experiments are fecal shedding of Bp and survival to day 60 after inoculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fecal pellets collected twice weekly; fecal bacterial counts determined using modified Ashdown medium; mice weighed daily and observed for clinical signs; ill mice euthanized with organ cultures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational criteria for classifying high vs low virulence isolates
rubrics_metrics.description: High-virulence isolates: evidence of heavy intestinal infection (persistent fecal shedding, high intestinal titers), significant weight loss, and short survival times; Low-virulence isolates: do not cause death, weight loss, or persistent fecal shedding during the 60-day observation period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect to identify 3–5 high and 3–5 low virulence isolates using these criteria; plan to adjust challenge dose if initial screening at 10^3 CFU does not distinguish phenotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of oral challenge dose and inoculation method
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a low-dose oral challenge model (initially 10^3 CFU in 200 µl delivered by gavage) in BALB/c mice to screen isolates; gavage used to assure delivery deep into the esophagus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dose selection based on prior experience indicating 10^3 CFU distinguishes enteric from non-enteric isolates; contingency to adjust dose upward/downward depending on initial results.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vitro assays to correlate with in vivo virulence
rubrics_metrics.description: Use mouse primary intestinal epithelial (mIE2) and RAW267.2 macrophage cell lines to evaluate invasion and cytopathicity: infect at MOI 5 for 1h, wash, incubate with ceftazidime to kill extracellular bacteria, lyse and quantify intracellular bacteria; cytopathicity assessed after 24h with MTT or trypan blue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen the 3 most and 3 least virulent isolates identified in vivo; compare invasion statistically (non-parametric ANOVA); interpret whether invasion correlates with virulence or suggests alternative mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of fluorescently labeled bacteria and cell-identity assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Engineered GFP/RFP-expressing Bp strains will be used with confocal microscopy and flow cytometry to identify infected intestinal target cells over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time points: d1, d3, d7, d14, d30; dual-label IHC markers listed (F4/80, Ly6-G, cytokeratin, CD11b, Ly6-C, CD3, CD11c, DEC-205); multicolor flow cytometry as complementary method; contingency: increase inoculum or use anti-capsule antibody if labeling sensitivity is low.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal sampling and blood dissemination assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect blood at multiple early and late time points (30 min, 1h, 3h, 6h, 12h, 24h, 48h, 72h, 7d, 14d, 30d, 60d) to evaluate Bp entry into bloodstream; use flow cytometry and blood culture after lysing WBCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Salmonella invasion occurs rapidly; identify GFP+ blood cells and use cytospin/confocal microscopy; expect early bloodstream appearance in CD11b+/Ly6C+ monocytes and later persistence in monocytes during chronic infection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment to test gut as reservoir via antibiotic depopulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat mice that have persistent intestinal colonization with oral non-absorbed neomycin (5–10 mg/mouse once daily) beginning 30 days after infection to depopulate intestinal Gram-negative bacteria and assess whether dissemination is reduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare incidence of disseminated infection between treated and untreated groups over 60 days; measure blood neomycin levels and determine MIC for Bp if positive effects observed; control for possibility of Bp resistance to neomycin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genetic model to test leukocyte-mediated dissemination (CD18-/-)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use CD18-/- mice (compromised monocyte/neutrophil migration) and WT C57Bl/6 congenic controls infected with very low dose (500 CFU) to assess whether dissemination from gut is reduced in CD18-/- animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sacrifice cohorts weekly and quantify bacterial burden in spleen, liver, lung; interpret reduced dissemination as evidence for infected-monocyte trafficking; alternative interpretations include non-cell-associated bacteremia or altered control of primary intestinal infection in CD18-/- mice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative bacteriology methods (modified Ashdown agar)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a modified Ashdown’s selective agar developed by the lab to culture and quantitate Bp from intestinal contents and feces, which suppresses commensal enteric bacteria while permitting Bp growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine CFU in small intestine, cecum, colon and feces (~10^3 CFU/g feces reported); medium is being evaluated for human clinical specimens in collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis and multiple-comparison control
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Kaplan–Meier survival curves and log-rank analysis with Bonferroni adjustment for comparing survival between isolates; use non-parametric t-test for two-group comparisons and non-parametric ANOVA and multiple means comparison tests for >2 groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group sizes (typically n=4–5) claimed to have 80% power to detect differences; in vivo experiments will be repeated at least once to ensure reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size, power, and reproducibility standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan to use a total of ~660 mice (500 BALB/c, 80 C57Bl/6, 80 CD18-/-); most experiments utilize groups of 4–5 mice, which prior experience indicates provide 80% power to detect differences; all in vivo experiments will be repeated at least once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical comparisons described; explicit commitment to repeat experiments to assure reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal species choice and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Use mice because they are the lowest vertebrate species appropriate to model enteric Bp infection and because substantial prior data exist in mice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justifies species selection as required for vertebrate animal section of grant; ties back to prior data and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal housing and veterinary oversight compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Animals will be housed in ALAAC-approved facilities at CSU with Lab Animal Resources oversight and at least one veterinarian on call at all times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies institutional facility and oversight to meet regulatory/ethical expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humane monitoring and euthanasia criteria (endpoints)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor mice 3× daily for first 7 days and 1–2× daily during chronic phases; euthanize animals showing >20% weight loss, reluctance to move, inappetence, and/or significant respiratory distress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method of euthanasia: inhalation of CO2 as recommended by the American Veterinary Medical Association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select agent compliance and institutional registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Project involves Burkholderia pseudomallei (a Category B Select Agent); CSU facilities are registered with CDC (entity number C20070924-0686) and possession/use of select agents is monitored by university biosafety officers. Transfer of select agents follows federal guidelines and permits (USDA import permits, CDC/APHIS Form 2, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms institutional compliance and describes required permits and biosafety oversight for select-agent research and transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency and pitfall planning
rubrics_metrics.description: For each aim, expected results are stated and potential pitfalls and alternate approaches are described (e.g., increase inoculum if infected cell numbers too low; use flow cytometry if IHC problematic; adjust oral challenge dose; measure antibiotic blood levels to rule out systemic effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly documents alternative tactics to address experimental failures, demonstrating risk mitigation and adaptability.
